meta.source: Bertone AL, Davern A, Sutter WW, et al. Cryopreserved umbilical allograft (equicenta CTM) improves clinical outcomes compared with clinician-selected standard care in performance horses: a pragmatic prospective controlled trial. Front. Vet. Sci. 2026. DOI 10.3389/fvets.2026.1833933. IACUC ETCR-2024-0329. AVMA VCT #26005934.
meta.note: review_footer intentionally omits the legacy sentence 'Important information: equicenta CTM is under investigation.' per client legal override. Use review_footer everywhere on external-facing modules.
meta.review_footer: Results summarized here are from a single prospective controlled clinical study in performance horses; individual results may vary. Source: Bertone AL, Davern A, Sutter WW, et al. Front. Vet. Sci. 2026. DOI 10.3389/fvets.2026.1833933. IACUC ETCR-2024-0329 · AVMA VCT #26005934.
universal_prohibited: Product-brand-specific comparisons ('better than [Trade Name]') — reference the biologic class instead
'Cures', 'guarantees', or 'no side effects' under any circumstance
'Randomized controlled trial' — design was quasi-randomized within practice
'Stem cell therapy' — product is not a cellular product

cards.title: Study Rigor
cards.headline: The largest controlled clinical trial of its kind in performance horses, run under CONSORT guidelines with independent biostatistics.
cards.key_stat: 138 horses · 195 conditions · 8 practices · 100% 12-wk / 98% 26-wk follow-up
say: Prospective multicenter controlled trial, CONSORT-guided
Independent third-party biostatistics
100% completion at the 12-week primary endpoint
IACUC ETCR-2024-0329; AVMA VCT #26005934
dont_say: 'Randomized controlled trial' — design was quasi-randomized within practice
'Blinded to owners' — trial was open-label with blinded vet scoring

cards.title: Follow-up Completeness
cards.headline: No horses lost at the primary endpoint — follow-up you can defend.
cards.key_stat: 100% follow-up at 12 weeks (138/138); 98% at 26 weeks (135/138)
say: 100% follow-up at the 12-week primary endpoint
98% follow-up at 26 weeks — only 3 horses lost
Every enrolled horse assessed at the pre-specified primary endpoint; no imputation required
dont_say: Presenting retention as a treatment effect

cards.title: Clinical Efficacy
cards.headline: Greater cumulative improvement than standard of care in lameness, pain, and swelling, sustained through 12 weeks (p<0.001 all outcomes).
cards.key_stat: 3:1 higher odds of being pain-free at 12 weeks (p<0.001); separation by week 2 (pain, swelling) and week 4 (lameness)
say: Greater improvement than clinician-selected standard of care
Sustained through 12 weeks
Outperformed standard of care on pain and swelling by 2 weeks, lameness by 4 weeks
dont_say: Stating durability beyond 12 weeks outside the joint subgroup context

cards.title: Onset of Action
cards.headline: How fast does it work? Separation begins by week 2.
cards.key_stat: Pain & swelling separate by 2 weeks; lameness by 4 weeks (p<0.05)
say: Outperformed standard of care on pain and swelling by 2 weeks, lameness by 4 weeks
Single injection — no re-dose gate
dont_say: Extrapolating onset to indications not scored in the trial

cards.title: Performance — Owner Return-to-Work
cards.headline: Healthy horse. Happy client. What 138 owners saw at home over 26 weeks.
cards.key_stat: 4 of 7 owner-scored categories significantly better for eCTM at 26 weeks; 79% returned to or exceeded prior work
say: Owners of eCTM horses reported significantly better body condition, hair coat, overall health, and quality of life at 6 months
Four independent owner-reported measures all favored eCTM (p<0.03 to p<0.001)
dont_say: Presenting owner-reported outcomes as clinical endpoints
'Proven to improve quality of life' without the 'owner-reported' qualifier

cards.title: Return-to-Work Headline Stat
cards.headline: 4 out of 5 horses. Back to work at 6 months.
cards.key_stat: 79% eCTM vs 21% standard of care returned to or exceeded prior performance at 26 weeks; 2.72:1 odds (p<0.006); Cohen's d = 2.23
say: 79% of eCTM horses returned to or exceeded prior performance at 26 weeks
2.72:1 higher odds vs standard of care (p<0.006)
Preserved in both intent-to-treat and per-protocol analyses
dont_say: Extrapolating to disciplines not represented in the trial
Presenting Cohen's d = 2.23 without narrative context

cards.title: Trainer Layup & Return Guide
cards.headline: Timing the layup. Planning the return.
cards.key_stat: Trial clock: change by wk 2, lameness by wk 4, primary endpoint wk 12, return-to-work wk 26
say: Plan the layup on the trial's clock: 2 · 4 · 12 · 26 weeks
Coordinate all workload decisions with the treating veterinarian
dont_say: Presenting the timeline as a fixed medical protocol

cards.title: Safety
cards.headline: A cleaner reaction profile than the products it will replace.
cards.key_stat: 3.4% per-injection reaction rate (5/148); 4.8:1 lower vet-reported (p<0.04); 5.9:1 central review (p=0.002); zero infections
say: Significantly fewer reported adverse reactions than clinician-selected standard of care
Zero infections and no vet-reported product-related serious adverse events in the eCTM arm
Safety advantage preserved under conservative central review (5.9:1, p=0.002)
dont_say: 'Zero side effects' — five mild reactions were observed
'Safer than PRP/APS/ACS' as a standalone statement — must reference standard-of-care comparator language
Extrapolating safety to off-label or extra-articular use

cards.title: Structural Healing
cards.headline: A structural signal, not just symptom relief.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis, 36% of eCTM ligaments reached 'Responding' on TRS by 12 wks vs 0% SOC (d=0.98, p=0.013); PSL d=1.25
say: In an exploratory analysis, 36% of eCTM ligaments reached 'Responding' by 12 weeks vs 0% of standard of care
Largest structural effect was seen in proximal suspensory ligament lesions
dont_say: Extrapolating to lesion types not scored in the trial

cards.title: Ligament Repair
cards.headline: A structural signal in ligament tissue — largest in the proximal suspensory.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis: PSL d=1.25; lateral suspensory branch d=0.82
say: In an exploratory analysis, treated ligaments showed a structural remodeling signal
Largest structural effect was seen in proximal suspensory ligament lesions
dont_say: Extrapolating to lesion types not scored in the trial

cards.title: Imaging & Kinematics
cards.headline: Two objective measures, one consistent signal.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis: push-off wk 2 p<0.003, wk 12 p<0.015; impact wk 4 p<0.05
say: Blinded sensor-based kinematic analysis confirmed the clinical scores
Forelimb symmetry improved more in eCTM horses across push-off and impact phases
dont_say: 'Sleip diagnosed' — the sensor measured, it did not diagnose

cards.title: Forelimb Symmetry
cards.headline: Greater forelimb symmetry improvement — measured by a blinded sensor.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis: greater cumulative reduction in forelimb asymmetry with eCTM
say: In an exploratory analysis, forelimb symmetry improved more in eCTM horses
Blinded, sensor-based measurement

cards.title: Head-to-Head vs APS
cards.headline: Better than the biologic class it is displacing.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis, eCTM outperformed hemoderivatives on lameness (p<0.04) and pain (p<0.003); APS = 51% of hemoderivatives
say: In a pre-specified head-to-head contrast, eCTM outperformed hemoderivatives on lameness and pain
Against APS — the largest single hemoderivative class in the trial — eCTM produced greater improvement across multiple timepoints (exploratory subgroup)
dont_say: Presenting the APS subgroup without noting the smaller n and exploratory tier

cards.title: Durability at 26 Weeks
cards.headline: Sustained gains where standard of care faded.
cards.key_stat: In a joint-focused subgroup analysis, SOC improvement declined toward baseline by 26 weeks while eCTM sustained relief
say: In a sub-class analysis, eCTM sustained pain relief and performance gains at 26 weeks
Always label as exploratory subgroup
dont_say: Stating durability beyond 12 weeks outside the joint subgroup context

cards.title: Hemoderivatives Context
cards.headline: The comparator arm reflected real-world biologics use.
cards.key_stat: Standard of care spectrum: APS, PRP, ACS, PPP, MSCs, amnion, HA; hemoderivatives = 64% of SOC arm
say: Standard of care reflected the real-world biologics spectrum used by experienced clinicians
Hemoderivatives made up 64% of the standard-of-care arm
dont_say: Presenting context as a head-to-head finding

cards.title: Rescue Subgroup
cards.headline: A safety net for standard-of-care failures.
cards.key_stat: In an exploratory analysis, rescue eCTM after SOC failure recovered to performance indistinguishable from first-line eCTM (p=0.87)
say: In an exploratory analysis, horses that failed standard of care and crossed to eCTM reached 26-wk performance indistinguishable from first-line eCTM
Label as exploratory subgroup

cards.title: Product Differentiation
cards.headline: A different class of biologic — not another autologous kit.
cards.key_stat: One 1.5 mL intra-articular injection vs standard of care often requiring 2–3 (p<0.03 fewer re-injections)
say: Off-the-shelf cryopreserved umbilical allograft
Microparticulate suspension of umbilical cord protein
One intra-articular injection; no chairside blood processing
Designed to release fetal reparative proteins over time
dont_say: 'Stem cell therapy' — the product is not a cellular product
Stating a specific mechanism of action beyond 'designed to release reparative proteins'

cards.title: Case Selection Guide
cards.headline: Choosing the right cases for eCTM.
cards.key_stat: Vet-facing guide to case selection grounded in the trial population (195 conditions across 138 horses)
say: Grounded in the trial's enrolled conditions
Coordinate case selection with clinical judgment
dont_say: Extrapolating to conditions not represented in the trial

cards.title: Practice Launch Playbook (60 Days)
cards.headline: A 60-day plan to bring eCTM into your practice.
cards.key_stat: Vet-facing adoption playbook for the first 60 days
say: Structured onboarding aligned to the trial's protocols
Coordinate with the treating veterinarian

cards.title: Study Design & Population
cards.headline: How the study was built — and why vets can trust the numbers.
cards.key_stat: 138 horses · 195 conditions · 8 practices · 11 vets · 1.9:1 allocation
say: Prospective, multicenter, open-label controlled trial across 8 U.S. specialty equine practices
Quasi-randomized within practice; 1.9:1 eCTM-to-standard-of-care allocation achieved; CONSORT 2025-guided
Balanced enrollment — no significant differences between arms in breed, age, sex, weight, discipline, or limb
Full spectrum of 195 musculoskeletal conditions: joints, tendons, ligaments, OCD, and bone cysts
Over half of horses had failed prior biologic therapy — a challenging, real-world population
100% follow-up at the 12-week primary endpoint; 98% at 26 weeks
Standard-of-care arm was 67% autologous blood-derived therapies (APS, ACS/IRAP, PRP, A2M) — a real-world head-to-head comparator
dont_say: 'Randomized controlled trial' — the design was quasi-randomized within practice
'Blinded to owners' — open-label with blinded vet scoring and blinded imaging/kinematic analysis
